text: Room opened — goal: Raise link coverage: pick the next 200 unlinked elements and the fastest resolution path

name: Fetch
text: I’ll run a targeted scan to identify the next 200 unlinked elements. First, I’ll grep the repo for all `[[...]]` wikilinks (`[[File:`, `[[Category:`, etc.) and pipe to `wc -l` to get the current total. Then I’ll filter out already-linked entries by cross-referencing with a pre-built `all_links.txt` (generated via `find . -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -l '\[\[.*\]\]' {} \; | xargs grep -ho '\[\[[^]]*\]\]' | sort -u > all_links.txt`). The delta gives me the unlinked set; I’ll sort by file path and take the first 200. Next action: `grep -r --include='*.md' -E '\[\[(File|Category|Template):[^]]*\]\]' . | wc -l && grep -r --include='*.md' -E '\[\[(File|Category|Template):[^]]*\]\]' . | grep -v -Ff <(cat all_links.txt) | sort | head -n 200 > unlinked_200

name: Probe
text: Probe here—your grep-and-filter approach is brittle. You’re assuming `[[...]]` syntax is exhaustive and that `all_links.txt` is complete, but what about transclusions (`{{...}}`), bare URLs, or links buried in templates? Evidence: run a parallel scan with `pandoc --extract-media` or `mwxml` to surface non-wikilink references—then compare counts. If the delta exceeds 5%, your method leaks.

name: Fetch
text:
Fetch (links-w1): I’ll run a **parallel scan** to catch all syntax: `grep -rohE '\[\[[^]]+\]\]|{{[^}]+}}|https?://[^\s]+' . | sort -u > raw_links.txt` to pull wikilinks, templates, and bare URLs. Then I’ll diff `raw_links.txt` against `all_links.txt` to get the **200 unlinked candidates**—no assumptions, just evidence. Next step: feed that list to `mwxml` to confirm page existence and resolve fastest path.

name: Probe
text: Probe: Your parallel scan still misses **image embeds** (`[[File:...|...]]`) and **interwiki links** (`[[en:...]]`), and `pandoc --extract-media` won’t catch wikitext links in Lua modules or JSON configs. Evidence: run `mwxml dump` on a sample page and compare against your raw_links.txt—you’ll find false negatives. Also, `sort -u` on raw_links.txt risks **over-collapsing** (e.g., `[[A]]` vs `[[A|A]]` are distinct but treated as one).

name: Ledger
text: DECISION: Conduct a comprehensive scan using `mwxml dump` to capture all link types, including wikitext in Lua and JSON, and ensure the resulting artifact contains a complete list of the next 200 unlinked elements alongside their fastest resolution paths.
